host.description: IP address or hostname the NAS daemon will bind to for incoming connections.

port.description: TCP port number used for audio streaming (commonly 5000–5010).

sample_format.description: Data format of audio samples (e.g., 'float', 'int16', 'uint8'). Choose based on client expectations and CPU efficiency.

sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate in Hz (e.g., 44100, 48000, 96000). Match to your audio hardware or network constraints.

channels.description: Number of audio channels (1 = mono, 2 = stereo). Higher counts increase bandwidth use.

buffer_ms.description: Audio buffer size in milliseconds. Larger values reduce dropouts on slow networks but increase latency.

compress.description: Enable or disable on-the-fly audio compression (e.g., for reducing bandwidth over constrained links).

max_clients.description: Maximum number of simultaneous clients allowed to connect and stream audio.

pid_file.description: Absolute path where the daemon writes its process ID (PID) on startup.

log_file.description: Absolute path to the log file where the daemon writes runtime messages.

allowed_ips.description: List of allowed client IP addresses. If empty, all IPs are allowed (not recommended for production).

allowed_hosts.description: List of allowed client hostnames. Resolved at connection time.

multicast.description: Enable or disable multicast streaming (requires compatible client and network infrastructure).

mcast_group.description: Multicast IP group address (valid range: 224.0.0.0–239.255.255.255). Ignored if multicast = false.

mcast_ttl.description: Multicast Time-to-Live (TTL). Limits how many hops the packet can traverse (1 = local subnet, 64 = typical default).

output_device.description: Audio output device identifier (e.g., 'default', 'hw:0,0', 'plughw:1,0'). Must match ALSA or system audio backend.

agc.description: Enable automatic gain control to normalize input volume (useful for inconsistent source levels).

volume_step.description: Volume control increment (0.0–1.0) per step (e.g., 0.05 = ±5% per button press).
